method: Each claim checked against the retrieved text of the ASHM genital HSV page. Doses and prevalence figures compared character by character.

claims.claim: Initial episodes may be severe and treatment should never be delayed while waiting for a test result
claims.source_text: Initial episodes may be severe, and treatment should never be delayed while waiting for a test result

claims.claim: Microbiological confirmation of diagnosis by NAAT is desirable but need not delay treatment
claims.source_text: Microbiological confirmation of diagnosis (NAAT) is desirable but need not delay treatment.

claims.claim: The auditable outcome is that 100% of patients presenting with an initial episode of genital herpes will be offered treatment
claims.source_text: 100% of patients presenting with initial episode of genital herpes will be offered treatment.

claims.claim: Do not screen asymptomatic people with serological tests for HSV types 1 or 2; serology is limited to specific situations and should be done with an infectious diseases specialist
claims.source_text: Serology: do not screen asymptomatic people with serological tests for HSV types 1 or 2. Use of serology is limited to specific situations where results will provide meaningful clinical information (e.g. an asymptomatic pregnant partner of a newly diagnosed person) and should be done in conjunction with and infectious diseases specialist.

claims.claim: Diagnosis is by HSV NAAT on a swab of the base of an ulcer or a deroofed vesicle
claims.source_text: Swab of base of ulcer or deroofed vesicle | HSV NAAT

claims.claim: HSV NAAT is very sensitive and specific but rare false positives and false negatives may occur, and a negative may not exclude HSV
claims.source_text: HSV NAAT - Nucleic Acid Amplification Test; a very sensitive and specific test; it is rare but false positives and false negatives may occur ... Negative - may not acquired HSV infection - see anogenital ulcers section

claims.claim: Self-collection of NAAT specimens at first onset of recurrent symptoms may be useful in patients who have failed to have confirmation when attending clinical services
claims.source_text: Self-collection of NAAT specimens at first onset of recurrent symptoms may be useful to confirm diagnosis in patients who have failed to have confirmation when attending clinical services.

claims.claim: Initial episode: valaciclovir 500 mg PO BD for 5-10 days; alternative aciclovir 400 mg PO TDS for 5-10 days
claims.source_text: Initial episode | Valaciclovir 500mg PO, BD for 5 -10 days | Aciclovir 400mg PO, TDS for 5 -10 days

claims.claim: Episodic therapy for recurrence, self-initiated at the first hint of symptoms: valaciclovir 500 mg PO BD for 3 days; alternatives famciclovir 1 g twice a day for 1 day or aciclovir 800 mg TDS for 2 days
claims.source_text: Recurrence: episodic therapy Should be self-initiated at the first hint of symptoms | Valaciclovir 500mg PO, BD for 3 days | Famciclovir 1g orally twice a day for 1 day or Aciclovir 800mg TDS for 2 days

claims.claim: Suppressive therapy: valaciclovir 500 mg PO daily for 6 months; alternatives famciclovir 250 mg PO BD for 6 months or aciclovir 400 mg BD
claims.source_text: Recurrence: suppressive therapy | Valaciclovir 500mg PO, daily for 6 months | Famciclovir 250mg PO, BD for 6 months or Aciclovir 400mg BD

claims.claim: Suppression in pregnancy: valaciclovir 500 mg PO BD from 36 weeks until birth; alternative aciclovir 400 mg TDS from 36 weeks until birth
claims.source_text: Suppression in pregnancy (see below for details) | Valaciclovir 500mg PO, BD from 36 weeks until birth | Aciclovir 400mg TDS from 36 weeks until birth

claims.claim: PBS streamline authority scripts are required
claims.source_text: NB - Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) streamline authority scripts required

claims.claim: Initial episodes may require a 10-day course if symptoms are slow to resolve
claims.source_text: Initial episodes may require a 10-day course of treatment if symptoms are slow to resolve.

claims.claim: The patient's ability to adhere to the recommended dosing frequency should be considered when selecting treatment
claims.source_text: The ability for the patient to adhere to the recommended dosing frequency should be considered when selecting the appropriate treatment.

claims.claim: Review the need for suppressive therapy 6 monthly as recurrences usually become less frequent and less severe with time
claims.source_text: Review the need for suppressive therapy 6 monthly as recurrences usually become less frequent and less severe with time.

claims.claim: Those with frequent recurrences such as 2 or 3 times per month, or immunosuppression, may require higher doses with PBS authority for the increased amount
claims.source_text: Those with frequent recurrences (e.g. 2 or 3 times per month) or immunosuppression may require higher doses (PBS authority required for increased amount of medication).

claims.claim: Seek specialist advice for patients living with HIV or immunosuppression, and for allergy to the principal treatment choice
claims.source_text: Seek specialist advice regarding patients living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) or immunosuppression. ... Allergy to principal treatment choice | Seek specialist advice.

claims.claim: Ongoing symptoms despite antiviral treatment should prompt consideration of other causes of genital symptoms
claims.source_text: Ongoing symptoms, despite antiviral treatment, should prompt consideration of other causes of genital symptoms

claims.claim: Management includes regular analgesia and topical lignocaine to reduce pain from erosions, fissures and ulcers
claims.source_text: Regular analgesia; Topical lignocaine to reduce pain from erosions, fissures and ulcers

claims.claim: Urinating in a bath or shower relieves superficial dysuria
claims.source_text: Urinating in a bath or shower relieves superficial dysuria

claims.claim: Neuropathic bladder requires urgent catheterisation and referral
claims.source_text: Neuropathic bladder requires urgent catheterisation and referral

claims.claim: Genital HSV is highly stigmatised and poorly understood in the community, and patient education addressing both clinical and psychosocial concerns is required at time of diagnosis
claims.source_text: Genital HSV is highly stigmatised and poorly understood in the community; Patient education to address both clinical and psychosocial concerns is required at time of diagnosis

claims.claim: The psychosocial impact of diagnosis can be profound but is often based on misinformation
claims.source_text: This can be profound but is often based on misinformation.

claims.claim: Community prevalence is 70-80% for HSV1 and 12-15% for HSV2, and giving these facts alongside the largely mild clinical effect is important for reducing stigma
claims.source_text: Providing facts about high community prevalence (70%-80% HSV1 and 12-15% HSV2) and largely mild clinical effect is important for reducing stigma.

claims.claim: More than 50% of primary genital infections are caused by HSV 1 in young people
claims.source_text: More than 50% of primary genital infections are caused by HSV 1 in young people.

claims.claim: Transmission can occur from someone unaware they have the infection, and symptoms can occur for the first time some days or years after acquisition
claims.source_text: transmission can occur from someone unaware they have the infection and symptoms can also occur for the first time some days or years after acquisition

claims.claim: Most HSV is asymptomatic or mild enough that diagnosis is never sought
claims.source_text: Most HSV is asymptomatic or mild enough that diagnosis is never sought.

claims.claim: Recurrences are more common in the first year with HSV 2
claims.source_text: Recurrences are more common in the first year with HSV 2

claims.claim: Refer to a psychologist for patients unable to accept the diagnosis, significantly distressed, or anxious about having the infection when tested negative
claims.source_text: Refer to a psychologist for support with patients who are unable to accept the diagnosis, are significantly distressed by the diagnosis, or anxious about having the infection when tested negative.

claims.claim: Neonatal infection is an extremely rare complication
claims.source_text: Neonatal infection - extremely rare complication

claims.claim: Neonatal transmission may occur in pregnancy, during delivery, or via skin-to-skin transmission in the post-natal period from oro-labial HSV
claims.source_text: Neonatal transmission may occur in pregnancy, during the delivery or via skin-to-skin transmission in post-natal period (via oro-labial HSV transmission).

claims.claim: The greatest risk of sequelae for the baby is when HSV is acquired in the third trimester or close to the time of delivery
claims.source_text: The greatest risk of sequelae for the baby is when HSV is acquired in the third trimester or close to the time of delivery.

claims.claim: Routinely commence HSV suppression from 36 weeks gestation in people who know they have the infection, with or without lesions, and earlier in people with multiple recurrent lesions during pregnancy
claims.source_text: Routinely commence HSV suppression from 36 weeks gestation in people who know they have the infection (with or without lesions). Commence at an earlier gestation in people with multiple recurrent lesions during pregnancy.

claims.claim: Contact tracing is not recommended for HSV infections, but patients may need support if they wish to disclose to current or future sexual partners
claims.source_text: Contact tracing is not recommended for HSV infections. ... Contact tracing is not recommended, but patients may need support if they wish to disclose to current or future sexual partners.

claims.claim: HSV is not a notifiable disease
claims.source_text: HSV is not a notifiable disease.

claims.claim: Test of cure and retesting are not required
claims.source_text: Test of cure and retesting. Not required.

claims.claim: Review a week after commencing treatment for the first time to evaluate response, complete sexual health testing deferred due to symptom severity, and educate about condoms, contraception, HIV PrEP/PEP, safe injecting, consent, cervical screening and HAV, HBV and HPV vaccination
claims.source_text: Review a week after commencing treatment for the first time to: Undertake evaluation of the response to treatment. Complete sexual health testing if unable to do so at time of initial presentation because of severity of symptoms. Educate about condom use, contraception, HIV PrEP/PEP, safe injecting practices, consent, CST and vaccinations for HAV, HBV and HPV as indicated.

claims.claim: Choice of suppressive therapy, episodic therapy or no therapy depends on clinical features including frequency and severity of recurrences and psychosexual complications of the diagnosis
claims.source_text: Choice of suppressive therapy, episodic therapy or no therapy depends on clinical features including frequency and severity of recurrences and psychosexual complications of the diagnosis (e.g. fear of transmitting the infection to intimate partners).

claims.claim: Other human herpes viruses including herpes zoster virus and Epstein-Barr virus can cause genital ulceration
claims.source_text: Other human herpes viruses can cause genital ulceration (herpes zoster virus [HZV]; Epstein-Barr virus [EBV]).
